editorial:
Ever wonder what happens to your pretend friends when you grow up? You get to see that magic in this story through Amanda and her best buddy, Rudger. They spend their days on wild make-believe quests, and the vibe is just pure childhood wonder. It feels like a warm hug at first, but things get interesting when Rudger finds himself in a world where imaginary friends go when they are forgotten. The movie does a great job of showing how it feels to be a kid with a huge imagination and the scary feeling of being left behind.

The pacing is steady, though some parts might feel a bit slow if you are looking for non-stop action. The best part is how it handles the emotional side of growing up without being too heavy. If you have kids, it is a perfect family pick, but adults will love it too.
endingExplained: In the end, you find out that the scary threat is actually the sadness and bitterness of forgotten friends. Amanda eventually grows up, but she does not truly forget Rudger. She remembers the love they shared, which saves him from disappearing forever. Rudger finds peace knowing he made a real difference in her life. They say a bittersweet goodbye, showing that while we grow up, the magic of childhood stays with us.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves heartfelt stories about friendship and growing up.
